scenarios.name: AI equity unwind
scenarios.story: The AI investment boom reverses: tech-led equities fall, credit spreads widen, the economy slows and the Fed cuts. Insurers lose on equity holdings and book lower reinvestment yields; slower payrolls and revenues shrink exposure growth; securities, D&O and cyber claims follow with a lag. Read the loss-ratio effect as indicative: the loading on financial stress is pooled within segments and identified mostly by the 2020 shock.

overlays.label: Professional-lines claims after a market bust (D&O, E&O, cyber)
overlays.basis: Assumption: securities-related claims surface 1-2 years after a market collapse. Weighted by how often a company's recent 10-K/10-Q filings discuss D&O and cyber.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical escalation
scenarios.story: A major conflict widens: the geopolitical risk index jumps ~70%, energy prices spike, rates and spreads rise and equities sell off. Political-risk, war, trade-credit and specialty marine and aviation books take event losses. Most of the underwriting hit comes from the labeled overlay, an assumption: past geopolitical spikes barely moved consolidated loss ratios.

overlays.label: Event losses on political-risk, war and trade-credit books
overlays.basis: Assumption sized like the 2022 war-related charges at specialty carriers. Weighted by how often a company's recent filings discuss political risk, war and trade credit.

scenarios.name: Climate-driven catastrophe years
scenarios.story: Two heavy catastrophe years in a row: an active hurricane season each third quarter and more secondary perils (convective storms, wildfire, flood) in the others. Property rates harden and E&S property grows.

scenarios.name: Social-inflation surge
scenarios.story: Litigation costs accelerate (larger verdicts, litigation funding, attorney involvement). Casualty loss trends outrun the assumptions behind existing reserves, so carriers strengthen prior-year reserves. The estimated litigation-cost channel is small; the reserve-strengthening overlay, an assumption scaled by each carrier's reserves, carries most of the hit.

overlays.label: Prior-year reserve strengthening (4% of net reserves)
overlays.basis: Assumption: 4% of net loss reserves is added over quarters 3-8. In loss-ratio points that is 0.04 x reserves / (6 x quarterly premium), so long-tail carriers with more reserves per dollar of premium take bigger hits.

scenarios.name: Everything at once
scenarios.story: All four stresses together: an equity unwind, a geopolitical shock, heavy catastrophe years and a social-inflation surge. Shocks add up; it is a tail scenario, not a forecast.
